---
title: "Week 8 Exercises - Git and GitHub"
---

Short, **ungraded** practice tasks - about 40 minutes. Companion reading: [Ch. 19](../book/chapters/19-git-github.html); reference: [App. H](../book/chapters/appendix-H-git.html). **HW2 goes out this week** (due Monday, November 30): analyze the data, write it up in Quarto, record your environment, and push the repository to GitHub - these tasks are its on-ramp, and version-controlling your term project from today is the best possible practice.

1.  Check that Git is installed (`git --version`), then introduce yourself: `git config --global user.name "..."` and `git config --global user.email "..."` (use the email of your GitHub account), and set `git config --global init.defaultBranch main`.
2.  Turn your course folder into a repository: `cd ~/projects/comptools && git init`. Run `git status` and read what it says.
3.  Create a `.gitignore` that excludes `data/` (large files do not belong in Git), the `.quarto/` working folder, and any `.DS_Store` files.
4.  Stage and commit: `git add .` then `git commit -m "First commit: course project skeleton"`.
5.  Make an account at <https://github.com> if you do not have one, and create a new, empty repository named `comptools`.
6.  Connect and push, following GitHub's "push an existing repository" instructions (`git remote add origin ...`, `git branch -M main`, `git push -u origin main`). Refresh the page - your files should appear. (First push failing with `Authentication failed`? Run `gh auth login` - see the lecture's authentication slide.)
7.  Edit your `README.md` locally, then - *before* staging - run `git diff` to see exactly what changed. Commit, push, and find the change in the **History** view on GitHub.
8.  Now edit the README *on GitHub* (the pencil icon), commit there, and `git pull` locally. Look at `git log --oneline` - you should see both commits, each with its short **hash**. Pick any two hashes and compare them: `git diff <older> <newer>`.
9.  Create a branch (`git switch -c experiment`), change a file, commit, switch back to `main`, and merge it.
10. Deliberately break something: delete a tracked file with `rm`, then rescue it with `git restore <file>`. This is the safety net that makes the rest of the course's habits pay off.
11. **Capstone**: render your project's Quarto report into `docs/`, commit and push, then enable GitHub Pages (Settings → Pages → branch `main`, folder `/docs`). Open the live URL - that link *is* your reproducible project, ready for the December 11 submission.
